| `plugins.routeros.<instance>.topology_only` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads only what is plugged into this switch or access point, and leaves its devices to the router. See [Show what is plugged in where](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/plugins/topology/index.md>). |

### plugins.openwrt

An [OpenWrt](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/plugins/openwrt/index.md>) router or access point.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads this source. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.host` | string | none, required | An address or host name, without a port | Where ubus is served. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.port` | int | `80`, or `443` with `ssl` | 1 to 65535 | uhttpd's port. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.user` | string | empty | An rpcd login | A login with the Jocasta ACL. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.password` | string | empty | Any | The login's password. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.ssl` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Uses HTTPS, once `luci-ssl` is installed. Without it, the password crosses the network unencrypted and Jocasta logs a warning. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.insecure` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Skips certificate checks, for uhttpd's self-signed certificate. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.timeout` | duration | `10s` | A duration | The longest one read may take. |
| `plugins.openwrt.<instance>.topology_only` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads only what is plugged into this access point, and leaves its devices to the router. See [Show what is plugged in where](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/plugins/topology/index.md>). |

### plugins.netflow

A [NetFlow](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/plugins/netflow/index.md>) listener for a router's flow exports.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.netflow.<instance>.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Runs this listener. |
| `plugins.netflow.<instance>.listen` | string | `:2055` | A UDP address, such as `:2055` or `192.0.2.10:2055` | Where the listener binds. |
| `plugins.netflow.<instance>.exporters` | list | none, required | IP addresses | The routers allowed to send. Datagrams from any other address are dropped. |

### plugins.technitium

A [Technitium DNS Server](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/plugins/technitium/index.md>) node.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads this server's query log. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.host` | string | none, required | An address or host name, without a port | The node's own address. A virtual address shared between nodes reaches one node at a time. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.port` | int | `5380`, or `53443` with `ssl` | 1 to 65535 | The web service's port. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.token` | string | empty | An API token | A token for a user granted Logs: View. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.ssl` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Uses HTTPS. Without it, the token crosses the network unencrypted and Jocasta logs a warning. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.insecure` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Skips certificate checks, for a self-signed certificate. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.log_app` | string | empty | An app name, as the Apps page lists it | The app whose log is read. Needed only when more than one installed app logs queries. |
| `plugins.technitium.<instance>.timeout` | duration | `10s` | A duration | The longest one read may take. |

### plugins.pihole

A [Pi-hole](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/plugins/pihole/index.md>) v6.

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads this server's query log. |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.host` | string | none, required | An address or host name, without a port | Where Pi-hole's web server is. |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.port` | int | `80`, or `443` with `ssl` | 1 to 65535 | The web server's port. |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.password` | string | empty | An app password | Empty reads a Pi-hole with no password set. |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.ssl` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Uses HTTPS. Without it, the password crosses the network unencrypted and Jocasta logs a warning. |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.insecure` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Skips certificate checks, for Pi-hole's self-signed certificate. |
| `plugins.pihole.<instance>.timeout` | duration | `10s` | A duration | The longest one read may take. |

### plugins.adguard

An [AdGuard Home](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/plugins/adguard/index.md>).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.enabled` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Reads this server's query log. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.host` | string | none, required | An address or host name, without a port | Where the web interface is. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.port` | int | `80`, or `443` with `ssl` | 1 to 65535 | The web interface's port. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.user` | string | empty | The web interface login | Empty reads a server with no login set. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.password` | string | empty | Any | The login's password. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.ssl` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Uses HTTPS. Without it, the password crosses the network unencrypted and Jocasta logs a warning. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.insecure` | bool | `false` | `true`, `false` | Skips certificate checks, for a self-signed certificate. |
| `plugins.adguard.<instance>.timeout` | duration | `10s` | A duration | The longest one read may take. |

## notify

Each destination sits under `notify`, keyed by a name you choose, and holds exactly one service block: `ntfy`, `webhook` or `http`. Which changes it is sent is picked on the account menu's Notifications page. See [Notifications](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/notifications/index.md>).

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notify.<name>.enabled` | bool | `true` | `true`, `false` | Sends to this destination. A destination is on unless it says `false`. |
| `notify.<name>.timeout` | duration | `10s` | A duration | The longest one send may take. |

### ntfy

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notify.<name>.ntfy.url` | string | none, required | The topic's URL, as ntfy shows it | Where messages are published, such as `https://ntfy.example.com/jocasta`. |
| `notify.<name>.ntfy.token` | string | empty | An ntfy access token | For a server that requires one. |
| `notify.<name>.ntfy.priority` | int | `0` | `0` to `5` | ntfy's priority, from 1 (min) to 5 (max). `0` leaves it to the server. |

### webhook

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notify.<name>.webhook.url` | string | none, required | An HTTP or HTTPS URL | Where the signed JSON POST goes. |
| `notify.<name>.webhook.secret` | string | none, required | Any | Keys the signature on each request. See [Check a webhook's signature](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/notifications/webhook/index.md>). |

### http

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notify.<name>.http.url` | string | none, required | An HTTP or HTTPS URL | Where the request goes. It can hold the service's token; it is never logged or shown. |
| `notify.<name>.http.headers` | map | empty | Header names and values | Sent with every request, such as `Authorization`. A `Content-Type` here replaces `application/json`. |
| `notify.<name>.http.body` | string | none, required | A Go template | The request body. See [Send to another service](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/notifications/other-services/index.md>) for recipes. |

# CLI

```
jocasta <command> [flags]

  serve              Start the web server and the sweep poller.  (default)
  scan <cidr>        Sweep a prefix once and print the result.
  ports [target]     Probe TCP ports on an address, a prefix, or the inventory.
  plugin run <name>  Read one configured source and print what it claims.
  version            Print build information.

  -c, --config       Path to the config file (default "jocasta.yaml")
      --log-level    debug | info | warn | error
      --log-format   text | json
```

Every command takes `--help` for its own flags.

## serve

```
jocasta serve                 # host and port from config
jocasta serve -p 9000         # override the port
```

Starts the HTTP server. When `scan.devices.enabled` is set, it also starts a poller that sweeps every network in `networks` on `scan.devices.interval`. When `scan.ports.enabled` is set, a second poller port-scans every address the inventory holds on your networks, on `scan.ports.interval`. Each enabled `routeros` and `openwrt` instance is also read for what is plugged into it, on `scan.devices.interval`. Each enabled `netflow` instance starts a listener for its router's flow exports, and an hourly prune deletes records older than their `retention` window, and devices you never curated that no scan has seen within `retention.devices`.

## scan

Runs one sweep and prints a table, or JSON with `--json`. With `--save` it also records the sweep in the inventory, under the name from `--source`, then `scan.source`, then this host's name.

```
$ jocasta scan 192.0.2.0/24
IP           MAC                VENDOR   HOSTNAME              RTT     DETAILS
192.0.2.1    00:00:5e:00:53:01  -        gateway.example      1.2ms
192.0.2.10   00:00:5e:00:53:02  -        nas.example          0.8ms
192.0.2.20   00:00:5e:00:53:04  -        -                    3.1ms   self (eth0)

$ jocasta scan 192.0.2.0/24 --save --rate 500 --no-resolve-names
```

The sweep uses a raw ICMP socket where it can and an unprivileged datagram socket otherwise, so it runs without root. A host with no reverse DNS name is asked for its name over mDNS, then over NetBIOS, then over DNS-SD, then over SSDP, until one gives it a name. `--no-resolve-mdns`, `--no-resolve-netbios`, `--no-resolve-dnssd` and `--no-resolve-ssdp` turn each off. With `--json`, each host also lists the services it advertises over DNS-SD.

## ports

Probes TCP ports with a plain `connect()`, so it needs no privileges and cannot change the target. With no argument it scans every current address the inventory holds on your networks: those in `networks` and the segments a router serves. A neighbour outside them, such as your ISP's gateway, is left alone. Each address is also scanned on the TCP ports its device advertises a service on and the ports recorded open on that device; give an address or a prefix to scan only that. `--ports` takes a spec like `22,80,443,8000-8100`; the default is a curated preset of about a hundred ports a homelab commonly runs. `--concurrency` caps how many connections are open at once (64 by default). `--save` records what it finds against the matching devices.

```
$ jocasta ports 192.0.2.10
ADDRESS      PORT   SERVICE
192.0.2.10   22     ssh
192.0.2.10   443    https

$ jocasta ports --save                      # every known address, recorded
$ jocasta ports 192.0.2.0/24 --ports 1-1024 --json
```

## plugin run

Reads one configured source without starting the server. Use it to check a credential or a firewall rule against the real router. It reads the instance even when it is disabled in config.

```
$ jocasta plugin run gateway
NETWORK           VLAN  NAME
192.0.2.0/24      -     Trusted
198.51.100.0/24   20    IoT

ADDRESS          MAC                VENDOR  HOSTNAME    STANDING     PRESENT
192.0.2.1        00:00:5e:00:53:01  -       gateway     DHCP_STATIC  true
198.51.100.10    00:00:5e:00:53:09  -       thermostat  DHCP_LEASE   true

$ jocasta plugin run gateway --json --save
```

After the devices it prints the source's topology: its ports and the VLANs each carries, the hardware addresses learned on each port, and its neighbours. A `topology_only` instance prints the topology alone. `--save` records both.

# Development

# Development

## Make targets

```
make build          # build to bin/
make test           # go test ./...
make e2e            # browser tests a pull request must pass (needs Chrome)
make e2e-full       # browser tests on every screen and account
make lint           # golangci-lint (installs it to bin/ on first run)
make dev            # hot-reload server via air
make gen            # regenerate sqlc models
make new_migration name=<name>
make oui            # rebuild the embedded MAC-vendor table
make htmx           # refresh the vendored htmx
make docs           # build the docs site and check every link (needs uv)
make docs-serve     # preview the docs site at http://localhost:8000
```

## Browser tests

`internal/web/e2e` drives Chrome over the real server, built with the `e2e` tag so `go test ./...` leaves it out. It needs Google Chrome or Chromium on `PATH`, or `E2E_CHROME` set to one.

Each page is drawn over four fabricated inventories (empty, a home network, one with extreme data, and one with no accounts), and each dialog, menu and inline edit it opens is drawn too. Every drawing is checked for sideways scrolling, clipped or overlapping text, small tap targets, small text, WCAG 2.2 AA failures (axe-core), script errors and failed requests.

`make e2e` draws every page as admin on a phone, a tablet and a laptop, in both themes. It takes about two minutes, and CI does not run it: run it before opening a pull request that touches the UI. `make e2e-full` adds every other screen and account; `scripts/release.sh` runs it before tagging.

A finding fails the run unless `testdata/known.json` lists it under an open issue. A fix deletes its entries. `make e2e-full` also fails on an entry that no longer matches anything.

The run also compares the first screen of every page on the home network with a stored picture in `testdata/golden/`: on a phone, a tablet and a laptop in light, and the laptop in dark. A picture fails when more than 64 of its pixels changed, which a single word added or lost exceeds. When a change is meant, store the new pictures and commit them with it:

```
E2E_UPDATE=1 make e2e
```

To see what changed, set `E2E_ARTIFACTS` to a directory: each picture that differs is written there beside a map of the changed pixels.

To look at a fixture in a browser:

```
E2E_SERVE=weird go test -tags e2e -run TestServe -timeout 0 ./internal/web/e2e/
```

To capture every page and read the findings, with no pass or fail:

```
E2E_AUDIT=$PWD/tmp/audit TMPDIR=$PWD/tmp go test -tags e2e -run TestAudit -timeout 0 ./internal/web/e2e/
```

`E2E_FIXTURES`, `E2E_ROLES`, `E2E_VIEWPORTS`, `E2E_THEMES` and `E2E_PAGES` narrow either run to a comma-separated list.

## Docs

The pages in `docs/` are published with [Zensical](<https://zensical.org>) to GitHub Pages, one version for each minor release and one for `main`. The `Docs` workflow builds every pull request that touches them with `make docs`, which fails on a broken link or anchor. A merge to `main` publishes the `dev` version, and a `v*` tag publishes that minor version as `latest`. Both are pushed to the `gh-pages` branch with the Zensical fork of [mike](<https://github.com/squidfunk/mike>).

When you change the docs:

- Add a new page to `nav` in `mkdocs.yml`, and to the `llmstxt` sections there, or the site leaves it out of the sidebar and `llms.txt`.
- A new plugin gets a page under `docs/plugins/` and a line in the table on the plugins overview. A DNS resolver also gets a column on [Record what devices look up](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/plugins/dns/index.md>).
- A new setting gets a row in the [configuration reference](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/reference/configuration/index.md>). `TestReferenceDocumentsEveryKey` fails until it has one, and fails on a row for a setting that no longer exists.
- Keep `docs/setup.md` and `docs/mcp.md`. Earlier releases link to their sections on GitHub, and each section there points to where it moved.

## Release

After CI passes on `main`, run the following. It runs `make e2e-full` first, so Chrome must be installed.

```
./scripts/release.sh v0.10.0
```

The script requires a clean working tree and a local `main` that matches `origin/main`. It checks that the tag is unused, creates an annotated tag, and pushes it to trigger the release workflow. It does not wait for the build.

## Layout

- `cmd/jocasta`: CLI entry point.
- `internal/scanner`: the ICMP sweep, and the reverse DNS, mDNS, NetBIOS, DNS-SD and SSDP lookups that name what answers.
- `internal/plugin`: sources beyond the sweep (RouterOS, OpenWrt, NetFlow, Technitium, Pi-hole, AdGuard Home).
- `internal/inventory`: the store, covering identity resolution, address handling, device classification and the change log.
- `internal/classify`: the rules that guess a device's type from its vendor, name and open ports.
- `internal/notify`: sends each finished scan's changes to ntfy, a webhook or a templated HTTP request.
- `internal/web`, `internal/api`: the HTML UI and the JSON API.
- `internal/db`: connection, migrations, generated queries.

Queries are SQLC-generated from `internal/db/queries/`. The schema is in `internal/db/migrations/`.

## Add a notification service

Most services take an HTTP request, and the `http` provider reaches them with a body template and no new code. For one of those, add a recipe to [Send to another service](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/notifications/other-services/index.md>). `TestRecipesInTheDocsRender` renders every recipe there, so a broken one fails the tests.

A service gets a provider of its own only when the `http` provider cannot reach it: it needs more than one request, a protocol other than HTTP, or signing a template cannot do. Each provider is in `internal/notify`, in a file of its own, as `ntfy.go` and `webhook.go` are:

1. Add a struct with `koanf` tags for its settings, and give it `Validate`, `Host` and `Send`. `Send` must not put a credential in its error. `post` covers a service that takes an HTTP request.
2. Add a field for it to `notify.Config`, and a line to `Config.provider`.
3. Add an example to `jocasta.example.yaml`, and a row for each setting to the [configuration reference](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/reference/configuration/index.md>).

The notifier, the settings page, the store and `cmd` need no change.

## Add a name source

Each name carries a standing, `dbtype.HostnameSource`, which says how it was learned. When sources disagree, the name with the higher standing is shown.

1. Add a constant for it in `internal/db/dbtype/enum.go` and add it to `hostnameSources`.
2. Give it a place in `HostnameSource.Rank`, and say why in the comment there. A name that resolves ranks above one a device only claims.
3. Word it for the device page in `standing`, in `internal/web/funcs.go`.
4. List it in [Name devices](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/naming/index.md>).

A sweep that asks devices for their names takes two more steps:

1. Add its lookup in `internal/scanner`, in a file of its own, and ask it in `enrich` in rank order. A query sent to each host is a `nameProtocol`, as in `mdns.go` and `netbios.go`. Any other lookup is a `nameLookup`, as `askSSDP` in `ssdp.go` is, or names hosts itself, as `browseServices` does with `dnssd.go`.
2. Add it to `HostnameSource.Swept`, so a lower-ranked lookup never replaces its name on the sweep's claim.

The column has no CHECK, so a new standing needs no migration.

## Screenshots

The images in [`docs/ui.md`](<https://pushkar-anand.github.io/jocasta/dev/ui/index.md>) are taken against a database of fabricated devices, never real network data: addresses from RFC 5737, hardware addresses from RFC 7042, invented names. Internet peers are well-known public services, so their organisations and countries resolve.
